books.title: The House in the Cerulean Sea
books.author: TJ Klune
books.blurb: A caseworker is sent to a seaside orphanage of magical children — and starts wondering whose side he's on.
books.aside: Softer than your usual. Do it anyway.

books.title: Piranesi
books.author: Susanna Clarke
books.blurb: A man lives alone in an infinite house of statues and tides. His journal doesn't quite add up.
books.aside: Short, strange, perfect. Trust me on this one.

books.title: We Have Always Lived in the Castle
books.author: Shirley Jackson
books.blurb: Merricat, her sister, and the arsenic that made the whole village hate them.
books.aside: Nobody in this one is okay. You'll love it.

books.title: Ancillary Justice
books.author: Ann Leckie
books.blurb: A warship's AI, stranded in a single human body, sets out to settle a very old score.
books.aside: Space opera, but make it a grudge.

books.title: Sea of Tranquility
books.author: Emily St. J. Mandel
books.blurb: A time loop threads a moon colony, a pandemic, and a forest in 1912.
books.aside: You'll finish it in two sittings. I've seen your pace.

books.title: Never Let Me Go
books.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
books.blurb: Boarding-school children slowly work out what they were raised for.
books.aside: It will hurt. Politely. In the best way.

books.title: The Little Friend
books.author: Donna Tartt
books.blurb: A girl in Mississippi decides to solve her brother's murder herself.
books.aside: Because you loved The Secret History. Obviously.

books.title: If We Were Villains
books.author: M. L. Rio
books.blurb: Seven Shakespearean actors, one dead classmate, and a decade of silence about what really happened.
books.aside: Dark academia with a body count. Your exact brand.

books.title: Babel
books.author: R. F. Kuang
books.blurb: An Oxford translator learns that language is the empire's real weapon — and he's been holding the knife.
books.aside: It's angry. Let it be angry.

books.title: The Atlas Six
books.author: Olivie Blake
books.blurb: Six magicians are recruited into a secret society. Only five will survive initiation.
books.aside: Everyone's insufferable. That's the point.

books.title: The Secret History
books.author: Donna Tartt
books.blurb: A tight-knit group of classics students commits murder — the mystery is why, not who.
books.aside: You already know. You've read it twice.

books.title: Circe
books.author: Madeline Miller
books.blurb: A minor goddess is exiled to a lonely island and becomes, slowly, someone to fear.
books.aside: She was never the side character.

books.title: The Song of Achilles
books.author: Madeline Miller
books.blurb: Achilles and Patroclus, before the war made them a legend.
books.aside: You know how it ends. Read it anyway.

books.title: Annihilation
books.author: Jeff VanderMeer
books.blurb: Four women enter Area X. The wilderness changes what it means to come back.
books.aside: Don't expect answers. Expect atmosphere.

books.title: The Starless Sea
books.author: Erin Morgenstern
books.blurb: A door with no walls leads to a library beneath the world, and a book with his name in it.
books.aside: More a place than a plot. Go anyway.

books.title: Mexican Gothic
books.author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
books.blurb: A young socialite visits her cousin's new husband's crumbling estate — and the house doesn't want her to leave.
books.aside: The house is a character. An unwell one.

books.title: The Shadow of the Wind
books.author: Carlos Ruiz Zafón
books.blurb: A boy finds one forgotten book and pulls on the thread of everyone who ever tried to destroy it.
books.aside: A book about loving books. On the nose, and lovely.

books.title: Rebecca
books.author: Daphne du Maurier
books.blurb: A second wife moves into a great house still entirely run by the first one — who's been dead for a year.
books.aside: The dead woman wins every scene she isn't in.

books.title: Fingersmith
books.author: Sarah Waters
books.blurb: A con artist and her mark fall in love. Neither of them wrote the ending they think they're in.
books.aside: The twist is worth the four hundred pages before it.

books.title: Convenience Store Woman
books.author: Sayaka Murata
books.blurb: Eighteen years behind the same register, and the only life that's ever made sense to her.
books.aside: Finish it on a lunch break. Think about it for a month.

books.title: The Ocean at the End of the Lane
books.author: Neil Gaiman
books.blurb: A man returns to his childhood lane and remembers a pond that was actually an ocean.
books.aside: Childhood, but the frightening kind.

books.title: Endurance
books.author: Alfred Lansing
books.blurb: Twenty-eight men, a crushed ship, and the coldest sea on Earth. Somehow a page-turner.
books.aside: Nonfiction. Boats. I know. Give it forty pages.

books.title: Norse Mythology
books.author: Neil Gaiman
books.blurb: Gaiman retells the Norse myths, from the first frost to the last battle.
books.aside: Loki is insufferable and you will enjoy every second of him.

books.title: Camp Damascus
books.author: Chuck Tingle
books.blurb: A model Christian town has a very literal way of curing its queer teenagers.
books.aside: Angrier than it is frightening, and better for it.

books.title: The Fisherman
books.author: John Langan
books.blurb: Two widowers go fishing at a creek that promises far more than fish.
books.aside: Quiet for a long while. Then extremely not.

books.title: The Bazaar of Bad Dreams
books.author: Stephen King
books.blurb: Twenty King stories, each with a note on how it came to exist.
books.aside: Dip in and out. Two or three will follow you home.

books.title: Nettle & Bone
books.author: T. Kingfisher
books.blurb: A convent-raised princess sets out to kill her sister's husband, collecting misfits.
books.aside: A demon-possessed chicken joins the party. Trust the process.

books.title: Home Before Dark
books.author: Todd Ritter
books.blurb: A woman returns to the haunted house her father wrote a bestseller about.
books.aside: The house is the least of it. Everyone lying about the house is the problem.

books.title: Hidden Pictures
books.author: Jason Rekulak
books.blurb: A nanny's small charge starts drawing pictures no child should be able to draw.
books.aside: The drawings are printed in the book. Sleep well.

books.title: Paperbacks from Hell
books.author: Grady Hendrix
books.blurb: A gleeful history of seventies horror paperbacks and their completely unhinged covers.
books.aside: Nonfiction that will cost you a fortune in secondhand paperbacks.

books.title: Project Hail Mary
books.author: Andy Weir
books.blurb: A man wakes alone on a spaceship with no memory and a planet to save.
books.aside: Yes, it is physics homework. You will still get attached.

books.title: Children of Time
books.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
books.blurb: A dying human ark ship meets the spider civilisation growing on its target world.
books.aside: You will end up rooting for the spiders. I don't make the rules.

books.title: Born a Crime
books.author: Trevor Noah
books.blurb: Growing up mixed-race in apartheid South Africa, where his existence was literally illegal.
books.aside: Funnier than it has any right to be. His mother steals every scene.

books.title: Midnight in Chernobyl
books.author: Adam Higginbotham
books.blurb: The Chernobyl disaster, hour by hour, from the people who were actually standing there.
books.aside: Reads like a thriller. It is very much not a thriller.

books.title: Bad Blood
books.author: John Carreyrou
books.blurb: A Silicon Valley darling promised to revolutionise blood testing. None of it worked.
books.aside: You will get angry. That is the correct response.

books.title: Say Nothing
books.author: Patrick Radden Keefe
books.blurb: A mother of ten is taken from her Belfast home in 1972 and never comes back.
books.aside: True crime that refuses to let anybody off easy.

books.title: Between the World and Me
books.author: Ta-Nehisi Coates
books.blurb: A father writes to his teenage son about living in a Black body in America.
books.aside: Short. You will not read it quickly.

books.title: Evicted
books.author: Matthew Desmond
books.blurb: Eight families in Milwaukee, and the business of putting people out of their homes.
books.aside: Follows eight families. You will remember all of them.

books.title: Red, White & Royal Blue
books.author: Casey McQuiston
books.blurb: America's First Son and the Prince of Wales go from enemies to something else.
books.aside: Sunny, filthy and completely unserious. That is the point.

books.title: The Love Hypothesis
books.author: Ali Hazelwood
books.blurb: A PhD student fake-dates the one professor everybody warned her about.
books.aside: Fake dating in a lab coat. You know exactly what you are getting.

books.title: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
books.author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
books.blurb: A reclusive film icon finally explains all seven marriages to an unknown journalist.
books.aside: You will guess the twist. You will be wrecked regardless.

books.title: Normal People
books.author: Sally Rooney
books.blurb: Two Irish teenagers keep finding and losing each other across four years.
books.aside: They could fix this by talking. They will not talk.

books.title: The Hating Game
books.author: Sally Thorne
books.blurb: Two executive assistants share an office and a mutual, escalating loathing.
books.aside: Enemies to lovers done properly. The elevator scene earns its reputation.

books.title: Confess
books.author: Colleen Hoover
books.blurb: A woman rebuilding her life walks into an art studio and complicates all of it.
books.aside: Hoover will hurt you. You already knew that.

books.title: Eleanor Oliphant is Completely Fine
books.author: Gail Honeyman
books.blurb: Eleanor has a rigid routine, a troubled past, and no idea she is lonely.
books.aside: She is not, in fact, completely fine. Stay with her.

books.title: I Fell in Love with Hope
books.author: Lancali
books.blurb: Teenagers on a hospital ward keep each other alive with stories and escape plans.
books.aside: It is very sad and it knows. Bring something to cry into.

books.title: The Silent Patient
books.author: Alex Michaelides
books.blurb: A woman shoots her husband and then never speaks again. Her therapist is sure he can reach her.
books.aside: You will see it coming or you won't, and both camps are insufferable.

books.title: Then She Was Gone
books.author: Lisa Jewell
books.blurb: Ten years after her daughter vanished, a mother meets a charming man with a daughter of his own.
books.aside: The kind of dread that arrives politely and refuses to leave.

books.title: The Guest List
books.author: Lucy Foley
books.blurb: A wedding on a remote island, a storm, and a body. Everyone present has a reason.
books.aside: Weddings and murder: two events where everyone pretends to be delighted.

books.title: The Sun Down Motel
books.author: Simone St. James
books.blurb: In 1982 a young woman disappears from a roadside motel. In 2017 her niece takes the same night shift.
books.aside: Motels at 3am are haunted whether or not there are ghosts.

books.title: Dark Matter
books.author: Blake Crouch
books.blurb: A physicist is abducted and wakes in a life that is his, except for everything.
books.aside: Read it in one sitting or don't start. There is no third option.

books.title: Uprooted
books.author: Naomi Novik
books.blurb: A corrupted wood takes a girl from her village every ten years. This time it takes the wrong one.
books.aside: Fairy tale in the old sense, where the woods actually want something.

books.title: The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue
books.author: V. E. Schwab
books.blurb: A woman trades her soul to live forever and is cursed to be forgotten by everyone she meets.
books.aside: Three hundred years of being no one, and then somebody remembers.

books.title: The City of Brass
books.author: Shannon A. Chakraborty
books.blurb: A Cairo street hustler fakes magic for a living until the night she accidentally summons something real.
books.aside: Court intrigue with actual fire in it.

books.title: Pachinko
books.author: Min Jin Lee
books.blurb: A Korean family in Japan across four generations, each paying for a choice made before they were born.
books.aside: Nothing shouts. It accumulates, which is worse.

books.title: Homegoing
books.author: Yaa Gyasi
books.blurb: Two half-sisters in eighteenth-century Ghana, one married off and one sold. Then their descendants, chapter by chapter.
books.aside: Every chapter is somebody's whole life. Pace yourself.

books.title: A Gentleman in Moscow
books.author: Amor Towles
books.blurb: A count is sentenced to house arrest in a Moscow hotel and spends thirty years never leaving it.
books.aside: A book about a man in a building that somehow never runs out of room.

books.title: The Nickel Boys
books.author: Colson Whitehead
books.blurb: Two boys at a Florida reform school in the Jim Crow era, and what the school does to them.
books.aside: Two hundred pages. You will not be fine afterwards.

books.title: Lincoln in the Bardo
books.author: George Saunders
books.blurb: The night after his son's burial, Lincoln returns to the crypt. The graveyard's dead have opinions.
books.aside: Unlike anything else on this shelf. Give it forty pages.

books.title: The Sympathizer
books.author: Viet Thanh Nguyen
books.blurb: A communist mole flees Saigon with the South Vietnamese general he is spying on, and keeps reporting.
books.aside: Furious and very funny, often in the same sentence.

books.title: Shuggie Bain
books.author: Douglas Stuart
books.blurb: A boy in Thatcher's Glasgow keeps trying to save his mother from drink, because nobody else will.
books.aside: Tender in a way that hurts more, not less.

books.title: The Tattooist of Auschwitz
books.author: Heather Morris
books.blurb: A prisoner tasked with tattooing numbers onto arriving inmates falls in love with a woman he marks.
books.aside: Based on a true story, which makes it heavier rather than lighter.

books.title: Daisy Jones & The Six
books.author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
books.blurb: A seventies rock band tells the story of the night they broke up, and none of them agree.
books.aside: Told as interviews. You will pick a side within twenty pages.

books.title: Where the Crawdads Sing
books.author: Delia Owens
books.blurb: A girl raised alone in the North Carolina marsh becomes the suspect when a local man turns up dead.
books.aside: Half nature writing, half courtroom. Somehow that works.

books.title: Punk 57
books.author: Penelope Douglas
books.blurb: Two pen pals who have never met finally do, and neither is who the other imagined.
books.aside: Dark, mean, and completely unembarrassed about it.

books.title: Lights Out
books.author: Navessa Allen
books.blurb: A woman looking for a hookup online matches with a man who hunts far worse people than her.
books.aside: You know exactly what this is. So does it.

books.title: Credence
books.author: Penelope Douglas
books.blurb: An orphaned heiress is sent to live with her guardian and his two sons in the Colorado mountains.
books.aside: Notorious for a reason. Check what you're getting into first.

books.title: Educated
books.author: Tara Westover
books.blurb: Raised off-grid by survivalists, she set foot in a classroom at seventeen and kept going to Cambridge.
books.aside: The bit that stays with you is how long she keeps going back.

books.title: When Breath Becomes Air
books.author: Paul Kalanithi
books.blurb: A neurosurgeon at the end of his training is diagnosed with lung cancer and writes about what is left.
books.aside: Two hundred pages and no wasted ones.

books.title: In the Dream House
books.author: Carmen Maria Machado
books.blurb: A memoir of an abusive relationship told in dozens of short chapters, each borrowing a different genre.
books.aside: The form is the argument. Nothing else does this.

books.title: I'm Glad My Mom Died
books.author: Jennette McCurdy
books.blurb: A former child actor on her mother, the industry that used her, and the years spent getting out.
books.aside: Funnier than the title lets on, and much harder.

books.title: The Anthropocene Reviewed
books.author: John Green
books.blurb: Short essays rating pieces of the human world — Diet Dr Pepper, sunsets, Halley's Comet — out of five stars.
books.aside: Perfect for reading four pages at a time before sleep.

books.title: Entangled Life
books.author: Merlin Sheldrake
books.blurb: Fungi, and the argument that they quietly run more of the living world than anything else.
books.aside: You will start noticing mushrooms. There is no cure.

tags.text: changes how you look at things

books.title: The spy and the traitor
books.author: Ben Macintyre
books.blurb: The KGB colonel who spied for Britain for a decade, and the exfiltration that got him out.
books.aside: Nonfiction that reads like a thriller because it actually happened.

books.title: Aurora
books.author: Kim Stanley Robinson
books.blurb: A generation ship finally reaches its new world, and discovers the hard part was never the journey.
books.aside: The starry-eyed colonisation dream, audited line by line by someone who actually did the maths.

books.title: Some Desperate Glory
books.author: Emily Tesh
books.blurb: Raised to avenge a murdered Earth, a soldier discovers the war story she was taught is a lie.
books.aside: A Hugo winner that opens like boot camp and ends somewhere you will not see coming.

books.title: An unkindness of ghosts
books.author: Rivers Solomon
books.blurb: On a generation ship run like a plantation, a brilliant outcast starts asking dangerous questions.
books.aside: Furious, strange and beautifully written. Bring a notebook and something warm to drink.

books.title: The Light Brigade
books.author: Kameron Hurley
books.blurb: Soldiers are beamed to the Mars front as light, and one grunt keeps landing in the wrong war.
books.aside: A time-scrambled war novel that trusts you to keep up, and rewards you for it.

books.title: Space Opera
books.author: Catherynne M. Valente
books.blurb: Humanity must prove its sentience at a galactic song contest, and sends a washed-up glam rocker.
books.aside: Eurovision in space, written at maximum volume. You will either adore it or bounce hard.

books.title: Revenger
books.author: Alastair Reynolds
books.blurb: Two sisters sign onto a treasure-hunting crew, and only one of them comes back unchanged.
books.aside: Space pirates cracking open booby-trapped worlds, with real teeth under the adventure.

books.title: To Sleep in a Sea of Stars
books.author: Christopher Paolini
books.blurb: A xenobiologist touches an alien relic on a routine survey and wakes an interstellar war.
books.aside: Eight hundred pages of first contact. Clear your weekend, then clear the one after it.

books.title: QualityLand
books.author: Marc-Uwe Kling
books.blurb: In an algorithm-run society, a machine scrapper tries to return a product the system insists he wants.
books.aside: Bleakly funny satire about the shop that knows you better than you do. Sound familiar?

books.title: The Water Knife
books.author: Paolo Bacigalupi
books.blurb: In a drought-shattered Southwest, an enforcer for Las Vegas hunts the water rights that could save it.
books.aside: Noir with dust in its teeth, and a near future that gets more plausible every summer.

books.title: Borne
books.author: Jeff VanderMeer
books.blurb: A scavenger in a ruined city adopts a strange creature she found on a giant bear.
books.aside: Yes, the bear is real, and it is the least odd thing here. Go with it.

books.title: Moon of the Crusted Snow
books.author: Waubgeshig Rice
books.blurb: A northern Anishinaabe community loses power in winter, then loses contact with the world below.
books.aside: The apocalypse told by a people who have already survived one. Quiet and devastating.

books.title: The Seep
books.author: Chana Porter
books.blurb: A gentle alien invasion makes anything possible, and costs one woman the wife she loved.
books.aside: A utopia with a grief-shaped hole in it, and it is over in an afternoon.

books.title: One Dark Window
books.author: Rachel Gillig
books.blurb: A girl who shares her mind with a dangerous spirit teams up with a highwayman to save her cursed town.
books.aside: The voice in her head has opinions. So does the highwayman.

books.title: The Goldfinch
books.author: Donna Tartt
books.blurb: A boy survives the blast that kills his mother and spends decades chasing the small painting he stole that day.
books.aside: Eight hundred pages. Not one of them wasted.

books.title: The Institute
books.author: Stephen King
books.blurb: Kidnapped kids with strange powers are held in a facility that insists it's all for the greater good.
books.aside: Nobody's coming to save these kids. They'll have to do it themselves.

books.title: The Only Good Indians
books.author: Stephen Graham Jones
books.blurb: Ten years after a reckless hunt, four friends are stalked one by one by something that hasn't forgotten.
books.aside: Some debts get collected. This one comes with claws.

books.title: Ninth House
books.author: Leigh Bardugo
books.blurb: A girl who can see the dead is recruited to police Yale's secret societies and their occult rituals.
books.aside: Dark academia with actual teeth. Mind the ghosts.

books.title: Lovecraft Country
books.author: Matt Ruff
books.blurb: A missing father, a road trip through 1950s America, and monsters that are sometimes the least of it.
books.aside: The ghouls are bad. The sundown towns are worse.

books.title: Slade House
books.author: David Mitchell
books.blurb: Every nine years, a strange house appears and someone new goes inside. Not all of them leave.
books.aside: Short book. Longest nine years of your life.

books.title: Ever After
books.author: Jude Deveraux
books.blurb: A woman inherits a Nantucket house full of secrets — and maybe a ghost with an agenda.
books.aside: The house came with more than she bargained for.

books.title: Fates and Furies
books.author: Lauren Groff
books.blurb: Twenty-four years of marriage, told twice — once by him, then completely differently by her.
books.aside: You will need to recalibrate everything by part two.

books.title: Killers of the Flower Moon
books.author: David Grann
books.blurb: Wealthy Osage families are murdered one by one in 1920s Oklahoma, and the case births the modern FBI.
books.aside: Reads like fiction. Isn't. That's the horror of it.

books.title: Permanent Record
books.author: Edward Snowden
books.blurb: The NSA contractor who leaked the surveillance state's secrets explains why, then goes on the run.
books.aside: Paranoid people were right. This is that story.

books.title: Can't Hurt Me
books.author: David Goggins
books.blurb: A man goes from an abused, obese childhood to Navy SEAL by refusing to accept his own limits.
books.aside: Motivational in the way a drill sergeant is motivational.

books.title: A Promised Land
books.author: Barack Obama
books.blurb: A president's own account of the campaign, the White House, and the decisions that kept him up at night.
books.aside: 928 pages. He was, it turns out, paying attention.

books.title: The Woman in Me
books.author: Britney Spears
books.blurb: Britney Spears tells, in her own words, what fame and a thirteen-year conservatorship actually cost her.
books.aside: You've heard the tabloids' version. This is the corrective.

books.title: One Last Stop
books.author: Casey McQuiston
books.blurb: A cynical grad student falls for a girl on the subway who turns out to be from the 1970s.
books.aside: Their meet-cute involves a time paradox. Adjust expectations accordingly.

books.title: The Spanish Love Deception
books.author: Elena Armas
books.blurb: She needs a fake boyfriend for her sister's wedding. The guy she can't stand says yes.
books.aside: Enemies to lovers, executed with zero mercy for your feelings.

books.title: Things We Never Got Over
books.author: Lucy Score
books.blurb: A runaway bride crashes into a grumpy small-town barber who does not want the drama she brings.
books.aside: Grumpy meets sunshine's more chaotic cousin.

books.title: Black Ties and White Lies
books.author: Kat Singleton
books.blurb: A struggling designer fake-dates his ex's older brother to fix the guy's playboy image, and it gets complicated.
books.aside: Fake relationship, real feelings, zero chill.

books.title: The royal we
books.author: Heather Cocks
books.blurb: An American exchange student falls for a British prince, and the tabloids never really let either of them go.
books.aside: Will and Kate, but make it messier and more fun.

books.title: The Raven Tower
books.author: Ann Leckie
books.blurb: A god narrates directly to a prince's servant, and neither of them can stop what's already been set in motion.
books.aside: The narrator is a rock. This works better than it sounds.

books.title: Red Sister
books.author: Mark Lawrence
books.blurb: A convent trains orphan girls to be assassins, and one of them was never supposed to survive that long.
books.aside: Nuns, but they will absolutely end you.

books.title: The Fifth Season
books.author: N. K. Jemisin
books.blurb: The world is ending again, and a mother searches for her kidnapped daughter through the wreckage.
books.aside: Won every award going. For once, deserved.

books.title: Kings of the wyld
books.author: Nicholas Eames
books.blurb: A retired band of mercenaries reunites for one last near-suicidal job to save a friend's daughter.
books.aside: Think aging rock band, but the reunion tour involves monsters.

books.title: The Priory of the Orange Tree
books.author: Samantha Shannon
books.blurb: An unmarried queen must produce an heir while assassins circle and an ancient evil stirs beneath the world.
books.aside: 848 pages of dragons and court intrigue. No, that's not too many.

books.title: The library at Mount Char
books.author: Scott Hawkins
books.blurb: A woman raised by a missing god has to use everything he taught her to find him again.
books.aside: Delightfully unhinged. Do not get attached to anyone.

books.title: Bunny
books.author: Mona Awad
books.blurb: An outsider in her MFA program gets pulled into her cliquish classmates' disturbing bunny-shaped secret project.
books.aside: The bunnies are not what they seem. Neither is anyone.

books.title: Lost Boy
books.author: Christina Henry
books.blurb: The real story of Peter Pan's island, told by the lost boy who becomes his greatest enemy.
books.aside: Peter Pan, but he's the actual problem.

books.title: Brain Damage
books.author: Freida McFadden
books.blurb: A surgeon takes a bullet to the brain, and what she can no longer remember might be the whole point.
books.aside: Her memory is broken. So is your ability to trust her.

books.title: Sleeping Giants
books.author: Sylvain Neuvel
books.blurb: A girl who fell onto a giant metal hand as a child grows up to help unearth the rest of it.
books.aside: Told entirely through interviews. Somehow, still a page-turner.

books.title: Once upon a river
books.author: Diane Setterfield
books.blurb: A supposedly dead girl wakes up at a riverside inn, and three different families insist she's theirs.
books.aside: Equal parts ghost story, mystery, and fairy tale.

books.title: The Trespasser
books.author: Tana French
books.blurb: A detective sick of thankless cases and office harassment catches one that's far weirder than it looks.
books.aside: Standalone case, same brilliant Dublin Murder Squad world.

books.title: The dry
books.author: Jane Harper
books.blurb: A man returns to the drought-stricken town that exiled him to bury the friend who might have framed him.
books.aside: Everyone in this town is lying. Some more than others.

books.title: The Tattooist of Auschwitz
books.author: Heather Morris
books.blurb: A prisoner forced to tattoo numbers on fellow inmates falls in love inside Auschwitz, and somehow, they both survive.
books.aside: As devastating as you'd expect. Read it anyway.

books.title: The Jane Austen Society
books.author: Natalie Jenner
books.blurb: In a small English village after the war, an unlikely group bands together to save Jane Austen's legacy.
books.aside: Austen fans will recognize their people immediately.

books.title: Ring Shout
books.author: P. Djèlí Clark
books.blurb: In 1920s Georgia, a sword-wielding resistance fighter hunts the literal demons hiding inside the Klan.
books.aside: Short, furious, and far more fun than a book about Klan demons has any right to be.

books.title: The Ballad of Black Tom
books.author: Victor D. LaValle
books.blurb: A Harlem hustler running errands in 1920s New York stumbles into powers older and hungrier than racism.
books.aside: It answers Lovecraft in his own genre, and wins.

books.title: The Last House on Needless Street
books.author: Catriona Ward
books.blurb: A shuttered house at the edge of the woods hides a secret its three residents cannot name.
books.aside: Trust nothing, least of all the cat, and then read it again.

tags.text: a cat who reads the Bible

books.title: The Spirit Bares Its Teeth
books.author: Andrew Joseph White
books.blurb: A trans, autistic medium in Victorian London is committed to a school that wants him obedient.
books.aside: Furious gothic horror that never once softens its edges for your comfort.

books.title: Welcome to Night Vale
books.author: Joseph Fink
books.blurb: In a desert town where the impossible is routine, two women chase a man nobody remembers.
books.aside: Funny until it isn't, which is the whole trick.

books.title: Monstrilio
books.author: Gerardo Sámano Córdova
books.blurb: A grieving mother grows a piece of her dead son's lung into something hungry and almost human.
books.aside: A tender book about a creature that eats things; somehow both halves work.

books.title: A Head Full of Ghosts: A Novel
books.author: Paul Tremblay
books.blurb: A teenager's breakdown becomes a reality show exorcism, and nobody agrees what was really happening.
books.aside: The ambiguity is the point, and it will keep you up arguing with yourself.

books.title: The Fireman
books.author: Joe Hill
books.blurb: A spore marks its victims with gold scales, then burns them alive; a pregnant nurse refuses to die.
books.aside: Seven hundred pages that somehow move faster than most three hundred.

books.title: Our Wives Under the Sea
books.author: Julia Armfield
books.blurb: Leah returns from the ocean floor changed, and her wife watches the woman she loves dissolve.
books.aside: Quiet, wet and devastating; do not expect a monster to solve anything.

books.title: Her Body and Other Parties
books.author: Carmen Maria Machado
books.blurb: Eight stories where women's bodies become haunted territory, funny and grotesque by turns.
books.aside: The one about the green ribbon alone earns its shelf space.

books.title: The Happiest Man on Earth
books.author: Eddie Jaku
books.blurb: A Holocaust survivor recounts seven years of horror and the deliberate choice to stay grateful.
books.aside: A hundred-year-old man explains happiness better than any self-help shelf, and he earned every word.

books.title: How to Be an Antiracist
books.author: Ibram X. Kendi
books.blurb: Kendi braids memoir with history to argue that being merely not racist is not enough.
books.aside: He indicts himself long before he indicts you, which is exactly why the argument lands.

books.title: The Jakarta Method
books.author: Vincent Bevins
books.blurb: Investigative history of the US-backed mass killings that quietly decided the Cold War's outcome.
books.aside: You will finish this and reread the entire twentieth century with different eyes.

books.title: Caste
books.author: Isabel Wilkerson
books.blurb: Wilkerson reframes American racism as a caste system, linking it to India and Nazi Germany.
books.aside: The kind of argument that rearranges the furniture in your head and leaves it there.

books.title: Never Split the Difference
books.author: Chris Voss
books.blurb: An FBI hostage negotiator turns life-or-death tactics into rules for ordinary bargaining.
books.aside: You will absolutely try the late-night radio voice on someone this week. Sorry in advance.

books.title: What My Bones Know
books.author: Stephanie Foo
books.blurb: A radio producer diagnosed with complex PTSD researches and reports her way toward healing.
books.aside: A trauma memoir built like an investigation, which somehow makes it far more hopeful.

books.title: The Argonauts
books.author: Maggie Nelson
books.blurb: Nelson braids queer love, pregnancy, and theory into a restless memoir about making family.
books.aside: Autotheory sounds forbidding until Nelson makes it read like a very smart friend confiding.

books.title: Why We Sleep
books.author: Matthew P. Walker
books.blurb: A neuroscientist explains what sleep does for the brain and what losing it costs.
books.aside: Read it early in the evening; it makes a compelling case against reading late.

books.title: Invisible Women
books.author: Caroline Criado Perez
books.blurb: How a world designed around male-default data quietly fails half of its population.
books.aside: Once you notice the gap in the data, you cannot unsee it in any room.

books.title: Bullshit Jobs
books.author: David Graeber
books.blurb: An anthropologist argues millions of pointless jobs exist and quietly corrode the people doing them.
books.aside: Dangerous to read at your desk, in the best possible way.
